We are probably all familiar with how Reddit works; one day the majority of users hate a celebrity or politician, the next day a new piece of information emerges which is enough to push the majority to love that person. This is how the upvote system works, it brings out the majority opinion. It is enough to make the entire attitude of the community appear to do a U turn in days. This is what we call an echo chamber.

Sometimes the majority opinion can be wrong. Though this is more unlikely when the percentage is higher, when it is wrong it is disastrously wrong. Some users get caught up in the group mentality so much they start harassing individuals in real life or even sending death threats. What if they happen to be misinformed as well? Then it becomes mob justice but on a global scale. A truly frightening thing.

It's frightening to imagine being one of a bunch of admins trying to control this beast which sometimes goes into a frenzy. There are thousands of people scrutinising every last word, and if the wrong thing is said it is guaranteed that it will be blown out of proportion and all those people will bring out their torches and pitchforks. In fact, on top of that, sometimes decisions the community will not like have to be made. Maybe we were not told the full story behind one particular employee's firing - for a company not to air its dirty laundry in public is simply professional.

Political opinions should never be censored. However if personal insults and death threats are removed isn't that a good thing? If Reddit was really keen on being self-serving they would have more quickly removed all the dissenting posts and the ones which pointed users to Voat. They haven't.

However one good reason to move from Reddit to Voat is to get away from all the paranoia, negativity and abuse by its users. In summary we should continue to use Voat and continue to speak freely but we should keep it civil.
